# "build the read-only view API with the Lime Tactical screen rollout, screen by screen").
#
# A screen asks one of these functions for what it shows and gets plain values back (numbers, strings, small dictionaries and
# arrays it may keep or change freely). Nothing here writes to the campaign, draws a random number or keeps state, so calling
# a view never changes a run, a save or parity. When a save field is renamed or reshaped, only this file has to follow it;
# the screens that read through it do not.
#
# The Nemesis (Muse's check of PR 349, condition 1): every Nemesis fact here starts from C.nemRead() (issue 364, PR 399), the
# campaign's read with no side effect, and the commander it returns is handed to the campaign's own rules (nemNodeIs,
# nemBeh, nemWarnLine, nemPanelData, nemFull, nemMeetingLine), which resolve nothing when they are given one. This file
# never calls one of them without a commander, and never calls nemActive or ensureNemesis: those resolve the commander
# first (nemActive migrates an old save and builds a missing record). The rules stay in campaign.gd; nothing is restated
# here. godot/campaign/test/map_readonly_test.gd proves the property itself: opening the map, the Dossier and the Map key
# never creates or changes the Nemesis record, the run, the save or the random stream, even when the record is missing.
#

# Death-only variation of the existing surface adapter. No R80 surface state changes.
# The running lights go out band by band: death_axis and death_span pick the direction (a cruiser bow to stern, a
# capital deck by deck from the top), death_steps holds (bands, delay per band, fade).
static func power_material(mat: ShaderMaterial) -> ShaderMaterial:
	var code: String = mat.shader.code
	code = code.replace("uniform float fx_power = 1.0;", "uniform float fx_power = 1.0;\nuniform float death_age = 0.0;\nuniform float death_start = 0.0;\nuniform vec2 death_span = vec2(0.0, 1.0);\nuniform vec3 death_axis = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);\nuniform vec3 death_steps = vec3(3.0, 0.055, 0.18);")
	var band := "floor(clamp((dot(fx_hull_p, death_axis) - death_span.x) / death_span.y, 0.0, 0.999) * death_steps.x) * death_steps.y"
	code = code.replace("clamp(fx_power, 0.0, 1.0)", "(1.0 - smoothstep(" + band + ", " + band + " + death_steps.z, death_age))")
	mat.shader = HULL.shared_shader(code)
	return mat

# GPU particle storage for the effects library.
#
# Every particle is static data on the GPU (start time, motion, colour, size, kind); the shaders work out its age from
# the effect clock, so the CPU never animates particles. Two containers share one vertex format:
#   Pool  : a fixed-size ring buffer in world space for one-shot particles. Emitting writes the particle's 20 floats into
#           the next slot (all of its vertices) and marks the range dirty; flush() uploads only the dirty range once a
#           frame (RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_attribute_region). The oldest particle is overwritten when the
#           ring wraps, so capacity is sized for several seconds of the heaviest fighting.
#   Batch : built once, then static, usually attached to a ship (looping particles: engine cores, breach fires).
# Attribute layout per vertex (checked on Godot 4.7.2): uv(2) uv2(2) custom0(4) custom1(4) custom2(4) custom3(4), 80 bytes.

		_burst(fx, p, axis, T, size, "vent", life, col, strength, 0.0, velocity, opacity, aspect)

# Sample the actual curved path at fixed intervals. Cap catch-up after a hitch,
# and let each short puff cool independently. There is no persistent hot ribbon.
static func _projectile_exhaust(fx, p: Dictionary, dir: Vector3) -> void:
	var lk: String = p["lk"]
	var k: float = p["k"]
	var last: float = p["last"]
	var rate := 10.0 if lk == "rockets" else 14.0

	var count := mini(3, int((fx.now-last) * rate))
	if count <= 0: return
	p["last"] = fx.now

# Scratch bytes for the float-word conversions: a fresh 8-byte buffer per call, never a shared static one, so rules code may run on a
# worker thread (the battle API's step() and threat_map()) while the scene thread converts floats too (Oct 26 review: the old static
# buffer was a data race). Costs about 0.2 microseconds a call.
static func _pb8() -> PackedByteArray:
	var p := PackedByteArray(); p.resize(8); return p

# ---- doubles as words ----
static func hi(x: float) -> int:
	var p := _pb8(); p.encode_double(0, x); return p.decode_s32(4)
static func lo(x: float) -> int:
	var p := _pb8(); p.encode_double(0, x); return p.decode_u32(0)

# First it proves the list is whole: every .gd file under godot/**/test/ is listed once, and every listed file exists.

# exit, on the time limit, or on any SCRIPT ERROR line in its log. Prints one line per check and exits 1 on any failure.
# The whole list also has a time budget (GODOT_CHECKS_BUDGET, 780 s; a healthy run takes about 200 s): a check gets
# 300 s or what is left of the budget, whichever is less, and a check the budget never reached is a FAIL, never a quiet

# The chart is tone mapped (ACES, then the contrast and saturation set in _ready), which washes a saturated colour toward

def finish(obj, band=0, bevel=.0009):
    # Retain the round 1 trim convention, but use physical bevels and weighted

    # Direct mesh work avoids thousands of context-wide operator updates.

# Ship recipe: read a ship's weapon list from the game's own data.js (plain Python; used by export7.py inside Blender and by
# check_export.py outside it), so hard point names always follow the rules file and never a copy of it.
import os, re
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); REPO = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..'))

def weapons(ship_id, data_js=None):
    """[(weapon kind, arc), ...] in slot order for the ship with this id in data.js; raises ValueError when it cannot be read"""
    src = open(data_js or os.path.join(REPO, 'data.js'), encoding='utf-8').read()
    m = re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])' + re.escape(ship_id) + r'\s*:\s*\{', src)
    if not m: raise ValueError(f'ship {ship_id} is not in data.js')
    end = src.find('}', m.end())
    w = re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])w\s*:\s*\[((?:\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*,?)*)\s*\]', src[m.end():end])
